newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Islamist leader Erbakan warns of chaos.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Islamist leader Erbakan warns of chaos.

text.p: Islamist opposition leader Necmettin Erbakan warned on Saturday that Turkey faced "chaos and confusion" under the new secularist government of Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz.
"Turkey is facing the danger of moving step-by-step towards chaos and confusion," Erbakan told a news conference after the new left-right coalition won a parliamentary vote of confidence.

"Turkey is in a state of uncertainty. Our people do not expect anything from this government," said Erbakan, who resigned last month under pressure from the army after a stormy year as Turkey's first Islamist leader.
His successor, conservative Mesut Yilmaz, clinched the vote earlier on Saturday in a parliament session marked by fights, shouting and one MP drawing a pistol.
Yilmaz garnered 281 votes to 256, with two abstentions.
Erbakan predicted that a key left-wing party would withdraw its support from Yilmaz's minority coalition once the government began backtracking on a promise to hold early elections in 1998.
"This government does not have the staying power so it is obviously not going to get anywhere," he said. "Let's see how many days it will last. You'll notice I am talking about days."
Most commentators say Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party would do well at early elections and wants to go to the polls as early as possible.
The party is facing closure for allegedly threatening Turkey's secularist system.
